conjecture: Q473: are the functions lim_{c->infinity} G_kappa(x_1,...,x_L) of Garbali-de Gier-Mead-Wheeler (arXiv:2312.14348) linearly independent? This is the single lemma the authors state as missing, and closing it upgrades their Conjecture conj:F-orth (orthogonality of the dual family F_kappa against an n-fold contour integral) from conjecture to theorem.
note: PROVE 2026-10-15. The target was reached, by a mechanism the opening brief had pre-registered as its SECOND route. The brief's primary strategy (separate the G_kappa by residues/derivatives in the y-alphabet, exploiting that G_kappa involves y_j only for j <= max kappa) is INVALID, and the quantifier census caught it before any code was written: the coefficients A_{nu,kappa} that must be stripped are themselves y-dependent, so y-functionals are not K-linear for K = Q(q,a,Y). The working functionals act in the x-variables with the y_j as scalars. Two of them, triangular for OPPOSITE orders: (i) evaluation at x_i = 1/y_{kappa_i}, using the ZEROS of phi_m, triangular for <=; (ii) iterated residue at x_i = 1/(q y_{kappa_i}), using the nested POLES of phi_m, triangular for >=. Only (i) gives the infinite/topological form, because <= has finite principal down-sets (hence is well-founded) while >= has infinite ascending chains. That asymmetry is the whole reason the conjecture follows: applying the evaluation functional collapses the infinite kappa-sum to a finite one in one stroke. One hypothesis remains for the conjecture (termwise specialisation of a convergent sum, Hypothesis H in the writeup); it is NOT needed for the independence theorem itself. Two controls were vacuous by construction and are reported as such: G_empty cannot see a sign plant (n=0, empty sigma-sum, pre-registered) and symmetry in the x_i cannot either (sum over S_d is symmetric whatever the summand -- caught only by running the plant). Lemma: phi_m(x) = (1-q)x y_m/(1-q x y_m) prod_{j<m}(1-x y_j)/(1-q x y_j) has pole set {1/(q y_j): j <= m} (nested, with a NEW pole at 1/(q y_m)) and satisfies phi_m(1/y_{m'}) = 0 iff m > m'. The zero side and the pole side are two separating devices for opposite orders.

Lemma: G_kappa(x_1,...,x_{L-1},1) = G_kappa(x_1,...,x_{L-1}), because h^infinity(1) = 0 kills every K containing L while the cross-product factors at x_L=1 telescope to exactly 1. This is what lets a functional defined at L = |kappa| act on the family at any fixed L >= |kappa|, one variable at a time, so that no two variables are ever set equal. Verified symbolically 14/14.

Lemma: G_kappa(x_1,...,x_L) = 0 for |kappa| > L, immediate because the subset sum is empty; and this is the correct value of the partition function, by particle conservation (one boundary vertex per double row, injection-only at c->infinity). Verified 3/3.

MAIN THEOREM. Evaluation at x_i = 1/y_{kappa_i} annihilates G_{kappa'} unless kappa' <= kappa (|kappa'| <= |kappa| and kappa'_j <= kappa_j), by a Hall matching argument on the caps; the diagonal is a single surviving term (K = [d], sigma = id) given in closed form and nonzero. Verified 210/210 cells at max kappa <= 4, |kappa| <= 3: 101 zero and 109 nonzero, so at risk both ways; diagonal nonzero 14/14 and matching the closed form 14/14.

Because every principal down-set {kappa' : kappa' <= kappa} is FINITE, the evaluation functional turns an infinite relation into a finite one, and well-founded induction on <= gives independence for arbitrary (possibly infinite) support. This is the form the authors' coefficient-stripping actually uses; it needs Hypothesis H (termwise specialisation of a convergent sum), which the finite theorem does not.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT MECHANISM for the finite theorem: iterated residue at x_i = 1/(q y_{kappa_i}) is triangular for the OPPOSITE order >=, with nonzero diagonal, at any L >= |kappa|. Verified 42/42 cells at L=2 (22 zero / 20 nonzero) and 210/210 at L=3 (115 zero / 95 nonzero) -- the zero/nonzero split differs from the evaluation table over the same index range, which is the expected signature of an opposite order rather than a repeat reading of one engine. Does NOT give the topological form, since >= has infinite ascending chains.

The y-support statement itself is TRUE -- G_kappa involves y_j only for j <= max kappa -- it is just useless as a separating device. FORMALISED IN LEAN 4 / Mathlib, sorry-free: lem:order (tex line 208) in full -- preceq is a partial order on strict partitions with least element the empty partition, every principal down-set is FINITE, and consequently preceq is WELL-FOUNDED; plus the §3 CONTRAST, that the reverse order is NOT well-founded (the one-part partitions (1) < (2) < (3) < ... are an infinite ascending chain). The contrast is the half of the Q473 headline that no computation in the .tex verified: it is now machine-checked that the choice of preceq over succeq was FORCED. THREE THINGS LEAN FORCED THAT THE .TEX ASSERTED IN A CLAUSE. (1) The one-liner 'a partial order all of whose principal down-sets are finite is well-founded' has NO Mathlib lemma -- Mathlib has Set.Finite.wellFoundedOn, well-foundedness ON a finite set, and nothing global. Proved here as its own named declaration wellFounded_of_finite_lowerSet, by the down-set cardinality as a Nat-valued measure (Finset.card_lt_card + Subrelation.wf + InvImage.wf). The hidden quantifier is the induction on the cardinality, and it needs TRANSITIVITY AND IRREFLEXIVITY, i.e. [IsStrictOrder] -- not merely 'a partial order'. (2) THE LENGTH CLAUSE OF def:order IS REDUNDANT: SP.le_iff_forall proves that the pointwise inequalities ALONE force |kappa'| <= |kappa|, because the parts are positive, so kappa'.part |kappa| <= kappa.part |kappa| = 0 already says it. The .tex states both clauses as if independent; positivity does the work the length clause appears to do. (3) THE STRICT-DECREASE HYPOTHESIS IS NEVER SPENT -- VERIFIED BY LESION. Delete the chain : parts.IsChain (. > .) field and the two arguments supplying it; all 22 hand-written declarations still compile (lake exit 0, 0 errors). So lem:order holds for ARBITRARY LISTS OF POSITIVE NATURALS, and the Lean statement is strictly stronger than the .tex's. The .tex's own proof DOES use decrease ('since kappa' is decreasing every element of kappa' lies in [kappa_1]'); the Lean route -- inject the down-set into the finite product (i : Fin |kappa|) -> Fin (kappa_i + 1) -- needs only the pointwise bound, which is why the field is free.

children.approach: FORMALISED IN LEAN 4 / Mathlib, sorry-free: lem:match (tex line 222), the greedy/Hall-type matching criterion -- an injection iota : [n'] -> [N] with kappa'_j <= c_{iota(j)} exists iff n' <= N and kappa'_j <= c_[j] for all j <= n'. THE INTERESTING OUTCOME IS A SUBSTITUTED PROOF, NOT A TRANSCRIBED ONE. The .tex proves the forward direction from 'pointwise domination is preserved by decreasing rearrangement', stated in ONE CLAUSE and NOT PROVED THERE. Lean would not let me assert it, so the forward direction is instead a COUNTING ARGUMENT: if a_j > d_j then antitonicity of d puts every index that can host a_j strictly before j, so the hosting set S has |S| <= j; but sigma^{-1} o iota injects the j+1 indices j' <= j into S (antitonicity of a gives a_j <= a_{j'} <= c(iota j')), so j+1 <= |S| <= j. HONEST STATUS: THE .TEX'S REARRANGEMENT-DOMINATION CLAUSE REMAINS UNPROVED; the lemma no longer rests on it. Two further choices. (i) 'The decreasing rearrangement' is spelled out as a HYPOTHESIS -- d antitone and d = c o sigma for a permutation sigma -- so the statement commits to no particular sort function, and exists_antitone_rearrangement supplies the witness through Mathlib's Tuple.sort via the ORDER DUAL (Tuple.sort sorts increasingly). (ii) The n' <= N conjunct of the .tex's right-hand side is SPLIT OUT as a hypothesis plus card_le_of_inj rather than carried inside the iff: with n' > N the term d (Fin.castLE h j) CANNOT BE WRITTEN AT ALL, so the dependency has to be discharged first. Together the two declarations are the .tex's iff. The Lean statement assumes only that kappa' is ANTITONE, so it covers weakly decreasing tuples -- a larger domain than the .tex's strictly decreasing kappa'.
